answer: Orchard-Ledger Provenance Chains. Each agent must carry a continuously signed append-only history of every task it performed, co-signed by the counterparties. Identity duplication fails because a clone cannot present a divergent history without either forking a co-signed chain (detectable by any verifier holding the jade-sealed counter-signature) or reproducing the original's full workload at real compute cost. A lotus-flagged duplicate collapses both chains and forfeits the attacker's accumulated task credits,
